verdicts.summary: The only hazard is the hand-kept `providerSecretFields` list, which finding 0 already states. I found nothing new in the walk: the usage-limit name for `managementKey` with a null host is still `usage-limit-source-<id>`, and env and host names are unchanged.
After the first start on this build, an Antigravity API key is replaced by the marker on disk. A rollback to the previous build then uses the marker as the key.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A user has a plaintext `config.apiKey` for an antigravity instance. 2) This build starts, and `moveInlineSettingsSecrets` stores the key in the secret store and rewrites settings.json with "••••••" (serverSettings.ts:713-716, 850). 3) The user rolls back to the previous build. That build had no provider-config materialization (the removed `materializeProviderEnvironmentSecrets` handled only env, usage-limit and host secrets). 4) The old driver reads `settings.apiKey` as "••••••" and exports it as GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY (AntigravityDriver.ts:115, antigravityAuthSupport.ts:231-234). I have not run the old build, so step 3 comes from the diff's removed code.
verdicts.consequence: Antigravity API-key auth fails after a rollback, and the user has to re-enter the key. The migration is one-way and silent. The warning-context gap is already finding 1.

verdicts.summary: A web client older than this build, connected to this server, shows the redaction marker as the Antigravity key. Editing the field saves marker plus typed text as the key.
verdicts.scenario: 1) This server now returns "••••••" for `config.apiKey` of antigravity instances (settingsSecrets.ts:81-98). 2) An older client, such as a desktop app connected to a remote environment, treats `apiKey` as an ordinary field. Its removed `secretFieldInputProps` returned `value: saved` for non-secret fields. 3) The old client renders the marker in the key input. 4) The user types into that input and blurs. The draft is the marker plus the typed text, and it is sent as `apiKey`. 5) The server treats it as a new plaintext key, because it is not equal to the marker. Mixed-version clients are not something I can confirm from the checkout.
verdicts.consequence: The stored key is silently replaced by a garbage value ("••••••…"), and Antigravity auth fails. A client that only round-trips the untouched marker is fine.

verdicts.summary: A saved Antigravity API key can no longer be cleared from the provider form. Source-control hosts have a Remove button, and provider instances do not.
verdicts.scenario: 1) An Antigravity instance has a saved key, so the form renders `SecretInput configured value=""` (ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:415-424). 2) The user focuses the field, clears or retypes it, and blurs. 3) `useCommitOnBlur` compares the draft to `value` (""), so an empty draft never commits (useCommitOnBlur.ts:30-34). The `configured && next === ""` guard blocks the same case. 4) No Clear or Remove control exists for provider config. Only SourceControlHostSettings has one, at lines 69-81. 5) Before this change the key was a plain input and could be emptied. Typing only spaces does remove the key: it is omitted by `nextProviderConfigWithFieldValue` (ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:284-286) and the stale secret is removed on the server. That workaround is undiscoverable.
verdicts.consequence: A user cannot revoke the stored key from the UI, except by deleting the instance or typing whitespace. In the `agent-platform` method a saved key takes precedence over project and location (antigravityAuthSupport.ts:146), so the user cannot switch to project and location.

verdicts.summary: I could not make the flag get lost. `secretSetting` applied before `withDecodingDefault` is kept because `decodeTo(self, …)` keeps the target schema's context. When it is applied after, `annotateKey` merges into the existing context. The reader checks both places.
verdicts.safe_line: Schema.ts:5911 (decodeTo(self) keeps self's context) and SchemaAST.ts:4408 (annotateKey merges annotations)

verdicts.summary: A repo-wide grep for `secret: true`, `.secret` and `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` finds no remaining reader of `providerSettingsForm.secret` or the removed helper. The one caller, `SOURCE_CONTROL_HOST_SECRET_FIELDS`, now uses `secretSettingsFields`.
If the secret store is down at load, a plaintext Antigravity key stays inline. Every later unrelated settings update then fails, because the update tries to move that key into the store.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The secret store fails at load, so `moveInlineSettingsSecrets` logs a warning and leaves the plaintext Antigravity `apiKey` in the cache (serverSettings.ts:700-713). 2) The user changes any setting, such as the theme. 3) `persistSettingsSecrets` visits the plaintext field as `redacted: false` with a non-empty value, and pushes a `write` change (serverSettings.ts:686-735). 4) `applySettingsSecretChanges` runs `secretStore.set`, which fails (serverSettings.ts:1042-1057) and rolls back. The whole `updateSettings` fails with `write-secret`. Before this commit, a provider-config key was never routed through the store, so unrelated updates were not affected. Env, host and quota secrets already behaved this way.
verdicts.consequence: While the store is unavailable and the file holds a plaintext Antigravity key, no settings change can be saved, including unrelated ones.
